prompt.context: Your client is Explorer Bank, a major issuer of credit cards. The company issues credit cards either under its own brand (e.g., The Explorer Platinum) or with partners (e.g., Southeast Airlines Advantage). A new airline, Alpha Airlines, recently approached Explorer Bank with a partnership credit card proposal.
prompt.question: How should Explorer Bank evaluate this proposal?

clarifying_info.q: What role would each party play in this partnership?
clarifying_info.a: Explorer Bank as the issuer will issue the credit card and provide all support; Alpha Airlines as the partner generally provides only branding and promotions.

clarifying_info.q: Does Explorer Bank have experience with airline co-branded cards?
clarifying_info.a: Yes. Explorer Bank has previous experience issuing credit cards with airline partners and currently partners with one other regional airline.

clarifying_info.q: Are there other revenue sources or costs we should consider beyond the obvious ones?
clarifying_info.a: All other minor revenue sources and costs not listed in the framework can be ignored for this case.

exhibits.title: Revenue and Costs per $100 Credit Card Spend
exhibits.shows: Two bar charts side by side. The left chart shows average revenue to Explorer Bank per $100 credit card spend broken into three components. The right chart shows average cost to Explorer Bank per $100 credit card spend broken into four components, plus a footnote about a fixed monthly cost per customer.

framework: 1. Determine market size: (a) existing Alpha Airlines customers — annual unique customers, credit card conversion rate; (b) card-driven new customer acquisitions — demographics, incentive structure

2. Estimate profitability: (a) Revenue — merchant/interchange fees, customer fees (annual, late), interest; (b) Costs — processing costs (e.g., Visa), partner revenue share, bonus for new customers, benefits (e.g., miles redemption), operational/service costs, credit losses
3. Assess risks: (a) impact on existing partners; (b) unexpected credit losses

questions.prompt: At a high level, do you think this type of partnership can be mutually beneficial? What are the benefits to Explorer Bank? What are the benefits to Alpha Airlines?
questions.guidance: Benefits for Explorer Bank: access to new customers; branding and promotion from Alpha Airlines; revenues from both Alpha Airlines-related purchases and everyday spend. Benefits for Alpha Airlines: stronger loyalty (customers with a branded credit card are more likely to select that airline); revenue share of credit card-generated revenues from Explorer Bank.

questions.prompt: What do you think are the major sources of revenue for Explorer Bank from this arrangement? What would the major costs be?
questions.guidance: Revenue: merchant/interchange fees; customer fees (e.g., late fees); interest on balances. Costs: processing costs (e.g., Visa network fees); partner revenue share paid to Alpha Airlines; bonus for new customers; benefits such as miles redemption; operational and servicing costs; credit losses.

questions.prompt: Based on Exhibit 1, how much does a customer have to spend per month on the credit card in order for Explorer Bank to break even on a customer?
questions.guidance: Candidate should read per-$100-spend revenues and costs from the exhibit, compute profit per $100 spend, then divide the fixed monthly cost per customer by that margin to find breakeven spend. A strong candidate will also comment on whether the breakeven figure is realistic for an airline co-branded card.

math.setup: Per $100 spend: Revenue = merchant fees + customer fees + interest. Costs (variable) = processing fees + partner revenue share + benefits + credit loss. Profit per $100 = Revenue − variable costs. Fixed cost = $15/customer/month. Breakeven spend = Fixed cost ÷ (Profit per $100) × $100.
math.answer: A customer must spend $1,000 per month on the credit card for Explorer Bank to break even. Note: $1,000/month on an airline co-branded card is largely feasible as long as the customer uses it for other travel purchases as well.

questions.prompt: What ideas do you have to help ensure that customers consistently spend above the monthly breakeven amount?
questions.guidance: See brainstorming section. Expect two buckets: Explorer Bank initiatives and Alpha Airlines initiatives.

brainstorming.prompt: What ideas do you have to help ensure that customers of Explorer Bank consistently spend above the monthly breakeven amount?

categories.name: Explorer Bank initiatives
ideas: Introduce additional rewards (e.g., incremental points for spend beyond a threshold)
Better reward redemption — more ways to use points/miles earned
Provide non-travel-related benefits to drive everyday spend
Incentivize customers to use the card for everyday purchases (e.g., purchase protections, insurance)
Create convenience features such as mobile and tap payments

categories.name: Alpha Airlines initiatives
ideas: Enhance cardholder benefits on Alpha Airlines flights (e.g., free checked bags, seat upgrades)
Discounts for other related in-flight purchases (e.g., drinks, meals)
Direct promotion at airports and in-flight (e.g., flyers reminding customers of card benefits)

recommendation: Explorer Bank should enter into a partnership with Alpha Airlines to launch a new co-branded credit card.
Both parties benefit from additional customer access and incremental profit.
Explorer Bank can be profitable as long as customers spend on average more than $1,000 per month, a figure that appears feasible for an airline co-branded card.
risks: Financial losses if average spend per customer falls below the $1,000/month breakeven
Credit losses if non-payment rates are higher than projected
Cannibalization risk if a majority of new Alpha Airlines cardholders had previously used other Explorer Bank credit cards
next_steps: Conduct demographic and segmentation analysis of Alpha Airlines customers to validate conversion assumptions
Finalize contract with Alpha Airlines and define individual responsibilities, including card promotion by the airline
